original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.

actual_scope: Rule out at most four paid one-way transfers for the five-source all-mask target with two arbitrary dirty connectors, freely chosen fixed source ports, ten complete B calls and 62 complete A readouts.
scope_change_reason: Addresses PR1438's explicit open four-transfer universal construction question in its already enlarged alphabet; adds a source-port partition proof, not a source-count extension inside the old alphabet.
bottleneck_link: Raises the minimum transfer cost from four to at least six for a proposed incidence-minimal recursive interface. A favorable completed budget must cover both dirty rows, port-specific children, every transfer, preparation, dispatch, routing, head and private-scratch restoration.
stop_rule: Stop at the four-transfer question; do not silently enlarge to six-transfer searches or infer a selected-supplier gain.
evidence: At exactly two calls per active A/B, four one-way transfers have at most 31 masks including zero for all source-port choices; hence at least six are needed for all 31 nonzero five-source masks. Written partition proof plus source-bound 945-pairing dependency, 37449 phase tuples, 26070 complete small skeletons, independent formal/dense restoration and paid transfer backend.
author: Gareth Davidson (@bitplane), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in mathematics, implementation, checks and writing; no independent human or proof-assistant review.

open_questions.question: Do six transfers suffice in the freely chosen source-port alphabet?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Determines whether the tightened necessary completed bill is attainable.
open_questions.first_step: Use the projection bound to eliminate mixed splits with at least three sources on the transfer source port, then inspect the remaining six-transfer cases with all dirty restoration.
open_questions.blocked_by: No six-transfer search or construction is included; restricted-source-port claims require their own verification.

open_questions.question: Does a concrete admitted supplier have a favorable complete port-specific bill?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Saving two expensive calls helps only if all transfer and storage/interface costs fit.
open_questions.first_step: Pin actual child prices, extra dirty row, clean scalar scratch, preparation, instruction access and dispatch before comparing an achieved old repair.
open_questions.blocked_by: A surviving construction and actual supplier admission are absent.

open_questions.question: Can an extra operator incidence yield a cheaper complete word?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This theorem applies only to exactly two occurrences per active operator.
open_questions.first_step: Analyze the 73-call boundary without assuming the old even-incidence property.
open_questions.blocked_by: The paired-readout and paired-source reductions must be replaced for extra incidences.
